reviewed_by: Codex GUI worker activation boundary review
reason: GUI enable/disable activates the normal Core PDF pool. The five feature Python files cover real owned PIDs/affinity, PDF equivalence/artifacts, restart/migration, stale saves, bounded queue/bytes, drain/repin/replacement, cancelled callers, legacy-thread ownership, startup failure/retry/cleanup and unknown observation recovery. Seven exact discovery/help/entry/product-index/Chroma-startup cases cover Butler integration and packaging. Four scoped frontend files cover activation/readback/polling, unknown counts, retry, conflicts and host changes. Exactly one real-Core production-LAN journey runs in each of eight permanent desktop/mobile Chromium/WebKit profiles. Separately, the conditional frozen-Linux job builds the actual executable and runs one enable/PDF/resize/restart/disable smoke; no Rust suites run. The owned 50-request large-PDF LAN burst tests bounded overload, live 3-to-1 resize, draining disable and ordinary API reads. No full suite is authorized.
exclusions: No real providers, external chat/tool/harness execution, GPU work, production deployment, physical devices or macOS/Windows activation. Linux affinity applies only to PDF workers. Native=0 means no Rust suites; one actual frozen Linux Core journey is selected separately. No unrelated Python/frontend/browser journeys.
